item.title: Claude Code Hooks: Every Event and How to Use Them for Memory (2026)
item.description:
What are Claude Code hooks?

Claude Code hooks are commands that run at fixed points in a session. You set them in a JSON settings file, and Claude Code runs them when the event fires, with no model choice involved. They are the only part of Claude Code’s setup that runs code on its own, which makes them the main way to save or reload memory automatically.

The Claude Code hooks reference lists 33 events. The ones that matter most for memory are SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PreCompact and SessionEnd.

item.title: Claude Code Settings: Files, Precedence and Key Reference (2026)
item.description: Claude Code settings are JSON keys in a few files. Put a key in the file that matches who should get it, and the higher-ranked file wins when two files set the same key. This page covers where the files are, which one wins, the keys people change most, and how memory settings fit in. Facts come from the Claude Code settings docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/settings and /settings-reference), read on 10 November 2026.
